items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Section headers ("// --- 8. UI Action Dispatcher ---") and names like updateAftersalePreview are clear. Business logic still uses single-letter names (`const o = state.orders.find(...)`, `l.time`, `t.className`), and the large inline HTML template strings are hard to read.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: One 3002-line file (cap applies). Refund allocation is copied into the UI preview (`sum += req.qty * oi.unitPrice * order.payable / order.subtotal`) instead of calling the shared function. The refundedQtyMap loop appears twice, and long markup-building code is mixed into the handlers.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Operations return {ok,error} and the UI shows errors as toasts. Hidden tests failed on seed data and on cart rejection of out-of-stock / over-stock items. Money uses float roundMoney rather than cents. There are magic numbers (`slice(0, 100)`, 3000ms toast).

items.name: Clerk workbench usability: amount breakdown, status hints, dangerous-action confirmation
items.name_zh: 店员工作台可用性：金额明细、状态提示与危险操作确认
items.evidence: pay, ship, cancel and restock all confirm before acting, and the paid-order cancel warning states the auto-refund amount. The after-sale modal shows paid, refunded and remaining amounts. Coupon stacking text and confirmation for reset/import are not visible in the code shown, so this area is thin.

items.name: Business logic lives in one place (UI and test API share it; integer-cent money)
items.name_zh: 业务逻辑集中且被界面与测试接口共用（金额按分计算）
items.evidence: The API and UI call the same addToCart, cancel and confirmReturn. The after-sale preview reimplements refund allocation in floats (`Math.round(sum*100)/100`). Money is float plus roundMoney, not integer cents.
